nodes.label: Constrained Query Vocabulary Expansion
nodes.rationale: graphify query matches via case-folded substring + IDF with no stemming or synonyms, so a question phrased in different vocabulary than the graph's node labels returns zero hits; expanding the query against the graph's actual label vocabulary first (never inventing tokens) prevents the answer from collapsing to noise.

nodes.label: prune_sources Deleted-Files-Only Rule
nodes.rationale: prune_sources must list only genuinely deleted files, never changed files, because build_merge already replaces re-extracted content by source_file; adding changed files to the prune set would delete the freshly re-extracted nodes right after they were merged in.

nodes.label: Honesty Rules
nodes.rationale: Never invent an edge (use AMBIGUOUS instead); never skip the corpus-size warning; always show token cost; never hide cohesion scores; never run HTML viz on >5000 nodes without warning - these exist to keep the graph's audit trail honest rather than optimized for a clean-looking output.

nodes.label: Confidence Score Rubric
nodes.rationale: INFERRED edges must pick one of five discrete values (0.95/0.85/0.75/0.65/0.55) instead of a continuous range, because production data showed models collapse a continuous range to a bimodal distribution (>50% at 0.5, >40% at 0.85+); a discrete rubric with named criteria is followed more faithfully.

nodes.label: Node ID Format Rule
nodes.rationale: IDs must be {full_repo_relative_stem}_{entity}, every directory level included, because this must match the ID the AST extractor generates independently; using only the filename or only the immediate parent directory creates orphan ghost-duplicate nodes when semantic and structural extraction disagree on naming.

nodes.label: graph.json Shrink Guard (#479)
nodes.rationale: to_json() refuses to write (returns False) when the new graph has fewer nodes than the existing graph.json, and the report/analysis sidecar are only written after a successful export - this prevents a failed or partial extraction from silently overwriting a good graph with a smaller, worse one.
